ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first such incident); record a driver violation for the deviation with no traffic reason (RD-2 / RD-4).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km, a deviation of 4.18 km billed at $1.4098/km = $5.89 [F1][F4]. The trace settles that the deviation exceeds 1 km, so RD-1's tolerance does not apply and the case turns on whether the single off-route segment is exempt [RD-1][RD-2].

The off-route segment, 21:43–21:50, drove JALAN BUKIT MERAH → KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD → TELOK BLANGAH ROAD → HENDERSON ROAD, adding 3.70 km and taking the car up to 1459 m from the optimal route [F3]. The trace settles there was no traffic reason on the replaced stretch: the AYE was at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and no incident is recorded, so RD-4 gives the driver no cover and the deviation is a violation if not exempt [F11][F13][RD-4].

On consent, the rider's only message before the segment, at 21:38, was "Whatever road you think is fastest, I trust you, don't need to follow the app", which the driver accepted with "Ok no problem" [F7][F8]. Read plainly, that is not a bare general "whichever way is faster" mandate covering the road chosen: the rider named the fastest road as the standard, the driver answered "no problem", and the record shows the detour did not serve that standard — the expressway was moving freely at 60–69 km/h with no incident and fair weather, while the car left it to loop through Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road [F3][F11][F13][F14][RD-5]. The rider named no road or place, so there is no named road to tie the segment to; the only words the driver offers are in a statement written after the trip, which is a claim and not timed rider consent [F10][RD-5].

No exemption therefore applies here. RD-3 fails because the rider named no stop or place and no stop was measured, and the driver's own after-the-fact explanation that he thought Telok Blangah Road would be faster is not consent under RD-5 [F3][F7][F10][RD-3][RD-5].

Amount: (4.18 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4098/km = $5.89 [F4][RD-2], the billed excess distance fare. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge is 1.0× so nothing is added under SURGE-3 [F5][F6][RD-2][SURGE-3]. The trace shows 0 prior upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's flag_account condition is not met despite the driver's other upheld disputes [F16][RD-6].
